name: Newton's Rings
desc: A convex lens pressed onto an optical flat, photographed close — the wedge of air trapped between them interferes with itself into Newton's rings, dark at the contact point and running out through the true reflected-light colour sequence until the source's coherence gives out and the orders wash to grey; the bench drifts, so the fringes march, and the optic under test can be swapped for a tilted flat, a cylinder, or a real aspheric with zonal error and astigmatism written into its interferogram.

energy.doc: lamp exposure on the plate (master knob)

scale.doc: macro magnification — high = a few huge orders filling frame, low = a dense field of fine rings

speed.doc: bench drift rate — how fast the fringes march and the lens rocks

density.doc: source coherence length — how many orders survive before washing to grey; also the Fizeau wedge slope

press.doc: pressure on the lens — flattens it, opening the radius of curvature so the rings spread

hue.doc: lamp colour cast over the 6-line spectrum; sets the laser wavelength in the mono styles

figure.doc: the optic under test: classic spherical lens, tilted flat (straight Fizeau fringes), cylinder (parabolic), aspheric (4th-order + astigmatism zonal error); 'auto' swaps it every section

seed.doc: bench seed — drift phases, astigmatism axis, plate grain and dust
